items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 8.6.2 at source lines 1600-1614, the wedge connectivity lemma: for pointed types (A,a_0) n-connected and (B,b_0) m-connected and a family P : A -> B -> type of (n+m)-types, sections f of P(-,b_0) and g of P(a_0,-) agreeing at the basepoints extend to a section h of P, with specified homotopies satisfying p = opp(q(a_0)) `ct` r(b_0). The proof (source lines 1615-1624) is not a direct application of one induction principle: it first manufactures the auxiliary family Q(a) := Sigma k, f(a) = k(b_0) together with its element (g,p) at a_0 (lines 1616-1618), then applies the induction principle for the (n-1)-connected map a_0 to reduce to a truncation-level statement about Q (line 1619), then identifies Q(a) with a fiber of precomposition along b_0 (lines 1620-1622) and invokes the same principle a second time for the (m-1)-connected map b_0, at which point the level arithmetic n+m is what makes the two applications mesh (line 1623). The two connectedness hypotheses are used at two different stages and on two different maps.
